name: Top-down tile city generator (roads, sidewalks, buildings, parks, points of interest)
description: Generates a repeatable 2D tile city from a seed: a grid of two-lane roads with edge ring roads, city blocks with a sidewalk ring and either a building or a park inside, plus a player spawn, police station, paint shop, mission landmarks, cash pickups, suggested pedestrian and traffic route requests, walk/drive cost tables and collision-check pairs for the spawn. Same seed, same city.
author: Skillpack contributors

provenance.license_check: Original code written for this pack; MIT
provenance.reference_values: tests/references.json holds frozen golden outputs of this original generator (regression only, not an external truth). Independent checks: the xorshift32 first output for seed 1 is 270369 (published sequence), and invariant tests check edge roads, block rings, connectivity, point placement and determinism.

region.notes: Game rules are illustrative defaults, not real-world rules.

audit.principle: code decides, model explains, craftsman (usta) approves

usta_approval.what_to_check: that the city size, block size and park share give a fun drive (not too empty, not a maze) and that landmarks are spread out.

external_audit.notes: Local tests only; no independent audit has been performed.

budget.enforcement: Raw CLI byte limit and POSIX alarm; strict schema, finite values and nesting checks; MCP subprocess killed/reaped after the timeout. One active calculation. Not a hostile-code sandbox.

dependencies.runtime: Python standard library plus jsonschema (schema check) only

data.logging: none; input contents are never logged or echoed in errors

mcp.instructions: One local deterministic tool. Explain its result and limits; the code decides, a human (usta) approves consequential use. No network access.

limitations: Manhattan grid only (no curved roads, highways, rivers or bridges). The last block on each axis absorbs leftover space and can exceed block_max. One building per block. Points are placed by the seeded generator and are not guaranteed to be interesting; the designer may change the seed. Modulo bias in randint is accepted (game use only).
port_notes: Original algorithm by Skillpack contributors. Random numbers come from xorshift32 (G. Marsaglia, 'Xorshift RNGs', J. Stat. Software 8(14), 2003; shift triple 13,17,5) seeded with the given seed (0 replaced by 0x9E3779B9). Axis split: edge road, then blocks of random width, final road on the far edge. Road connectivity is verified by flood fill and reported.
flow_role: Step 1 (harita): the first call of the flow; every later step reads its tiles and points.
